description: NextGen Space est une équipe multidisciplinaire participant au NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Notre mission est de concevoir des solutions innovantes qui rendent l'exploration spatiale, la science et les données de la NASA accessibles à tous.
summary:
We developed MissionSphere, an interactive, web-based NASA Mission Control simulator and serious game supporting both Solo and real-time 1–4 player collaborative modes, built with TypeScript, React, Three.js, Express, and Socket.io.
Addressing the Space Mission Design Game challenge, MissionSphere guides players through a realistic 15-phase engineering lifecycle modeled on NASA’s Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–6), CubeSat 101, and Systems Engineering principles. Teams take on four asymmetric roles—Mission Manager, Science Lead, Systems Engineer, and Operations Lead—to define requirements, negotiate trade-offs in a Mission Design Lab, assemble 2.5D spacecraft subsystems, configure 3D orbits (Earth, Moon, and Mars), pass a Mission Readiness Review, survive timed in-orbit crises, and compare their architecture against real NASA missions (SWOT, Landsat 9, Terra, PACE, LRO, and MAVEN). An isomorphic physics engine computes mass, power, solar irradiance, cloud penalties, link budgets, and science return in real time, supported by Space Mentor guidance.
MissionSphere matters because it transforms complex aerospace systems engineering into an accessible, hands-on experience—teaching learners that successful space missions depend not on isolated components, but on disciplined engineering trade-offs and cross-team collaboration.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS
MissionSphere is a web-based NASA Mission Control Center simulator and serious game (accessible immediately in the browser at https://mission-sphere.earth/ with zero installation or login). Before launching, an interactive 15-phase Roadmap introduces the entire mission lifecycle modeled on NASA's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–6). Players command all four Mission Design Lab disciplines in Solo Mode (or switch to a 10-second Quick Demo preset for rapid evaluation) across four structured acts:

  1. Act I — Concept & MDL (Phases 1–4, CML 1–2): Select one of 6 scientific scenarios (Earth Floods, Deforestation, Wildfires, Ocean Plankton, Lunar Polar Ice, Mars Atmosphere), configure budget/resolution/lifetime/risk requirements, review Mission Design Lab trade-offs, and choose a baseline architecture (ARCH A/B/C).
  2. Act II — Engineering & Orbit (Phases 5–8, CML 3–4): Assemble a 2.5D spacecraft (bus, GaAs solar arrays, Li-Ion batteries, S/X/Ka antennas, onboard computer), equip science payloads (C-Band SAR, HR Optical, Hyperspectral Spectrometer, Thermal IR), tune a live 3D Three.js orbit (LEO, SSO, GEO, Lunar, Mars), and pick a compatible launch vehicle.
  3. Act III — Validation & Flight (Phases 9–12, CML 5–6): Pass the Mission Readiness Review (GO/NO-GO) across 7 live telemetry gauges, monitor an animated launch sequence, survive 3 timed in-orbit crises (CME solar storm, orbital debris conjunction, thermal/sensor anomaly), and inspect sensor swaths and Deep Space Network ground passes (Goldstone, Madrid, Canberra) in 3D.
  4. Act IV — Science & NASA Match (Phases 13–15, CML 6): Review science return, receive a weighted score out of 1000 with Space Mentor diagnostic feedback, and match the player's spacecraft against real NASA missions (SWOT, Landsat 9, Terra, PACE, LRO, MAVEN) to unlock NASA Heritage badges.

In addition, a real-time 1–4 player Collaborative Mode (Express + Socket.io rooms, role locking for Mission Manager, Science Lead, Systems Engineer, Operations Lead, live chat/pings, and team voting) is implemented in the open-source repository and marked as "Coming soon" on the static web deployment.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT
MissionSphere transforms NASA Systems Engineering (SP-2016-6105), JPL Concept Maturity Levels (13-3547_A1b), and CubeSat 101 principles into a hands-on STEM learning experience for students, high-schoolers, educators, and space enthusiasts—available in both French and English. Players learn why space missions require disciplined quantitative trade-offs, technical margins, and crisis management rather than isolated hardware choices.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

  • Language: 100% TypeScript (.ts / .tsx) with an isomorphic shared physics, crisis, scoring, and Space Mentor rules engine running identically in the browser and on the server.
  • Frontend: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Zustand, React Router, Three.js (procedural 3D Earth/Moon/Mars & orbit visualization), Lucide Icons, and Web Audio synthesis.
  • Backend & AI (in repository): Node.js, Express, Socket.io, tsx, and Google Gemini API (@google/genai) with a deterministic rule-based fallback.
  • Hosting & Quality: Deployed on Vercel (https://mission-sphere.earth/), source code on GitHub, automated unit tests (PhysicsEngine.test.ts), and GitHub Actions CI.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

  • Coupled 7-gauge physics simulation: Real constraints directly affect design choices—such as ~70% cloud cover penalizing optical sensors on Floods (making C-Band SAR critical) and solar irradiance dropping to 43% at Mars (1.52 AU).
  • Socratic Space Mentor: Explains why a trade-off fails physics or budget constraints instead of giving away answers.
  • Automated NASA Heritage Matcher: Uses normalized feature vectors to compare each custom spacecraft with real NASA flagship missions and links directly to official NASA mission pages and source documentation at every phase.

FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM

  • Realism vs. accessibility: Translated real astrodynamics, orbital payload penalties, eclipse durations, and dB link budgets into color-coded telemetry (NOMINAL / WARNING / CRITICAL) understandable without aerospace expertise.
  • Bilingual & frictionless access: Full FR/EN toggle, pre-launch 15-phase roadmap, zero-login browser play, and offline-capable local simulation so judges and students can test every phase immediately.
  • Transparency & open sources: Every phase embeds direct links to the NASA references used (Systems Engineering Handbook, SmallSat SST SoA, GMAT, LSP, Orbital Debris Office, DSN Now) and uses procedural 3D/SVG graphics without copyrighted external assets.
